title: Replacement Remittances for Reopened Monthly Payments on Rural Home Loans — Servicing Desk Tool Card
content:
A replacement remittance on a Rural Home Loans loan is the remittance a member makes for a monthly payment that a returned remittance reopened, taken by phone and applied to that monthly bill: the reversed interest, principal and escrow shares are booked again, the fees it carries are paid from what is left in the order they were assessed, and anything beyond that goes to principal as a curtailment.

## Conditions on figuring

A replacement remittance is not figured until the ledger carries a late charge for every reopened monthly payment whose grace period has ended. A replacement remittance is figured only after the ledger carries a returned-payment fee for every returned remittance whose return reason calls for one.

Restated: while the ledger shows a reopened monthly payment past the end of its grace period with no late charge carried against it, or a returned remittance whose return reason calls for a returned-payment fee with no such fee carried against it, the replacement remittance is not yet figured.

## What applying the remittance does

The remittance is booked against the monthly bill named. The interest, principal and escrow shares that the bank return reversed on that bill are booked again at the amounts the reversal carried; out of what is left, the fees unpaid on the loan are paid one by one in the order they were assessed, each up to its unpaid amount; anything still left is booked as an extra principal payment (curtailment). The loan's principal, billed interest, escrow balance and unpaid fees move by the amounts booked, and the reopened monthly payment shows as paid in the payment history.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `apply_replacement_remittance_c604a214`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `loan_id` | the loan number of the Country Home loan, as returned by the home loan lookup | identifier |
| `bill_txn_id` | the reference number of the reopened monthly interest bill (the monthly payment being replaced), as shown in the loan's payment history | identifier |
| `remittance_amount` | the whole remittance taken from the member | USD to 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

## Return

A dictionary receipt: `bill_txn_id` (the monthly bill paid, a string); `interest_paid`, `principal_paid` and `escrow_paid` (the shares booked again, USD to 2 decimal places); `fees_paid` (fees paid in total, USD to 2 decimal places); `curtailment` (any extra principal booked, USD to 2 decimal places, 0.0 when none); `principal_balance` and `fees_due` (the loan's figures after the booking, USD to 2 decimal places); and `status` ("applied").

## Illustration of the order of application (hypothetical values)

A remittance of 2050.00 on a bill whose reversal carried interest 700.00, principal 831.20 and escrow 410.00, on a loan with two unpaid fees of 48.00 and 35.00 assessed in that order: the three shares take 1941.20, leaving 108.80; the fee of 48.00 is paid in full, then the fee of 35.00, leaving 25.80, which is booked as a curtailment.
